question: T4-06
answer:
Design basis and assumptions
- Cold plate inlet 35.0 C, outlet 45.0 C, so T_mean=40.0 C. KryoSol-45 at 40.0 C: rho=1200 kg/m3, cp=2000 J/kg-K, mu=2.40 mPa-s, Pv=22.0 kPa abs.
- The filter is placed on the pump discharge, downstream of the pump and upstream of the cold plate. This is a required layout choice: if the fouled FC-300 were on the suction side, its 53.08 kPa fouled drop would make NPSH_A negative. The fouled filter drop is included in total system head but not in the suction-line drop used for NPSH_A.
- The loop is closed, so the 0.50 m suction lift affects NPSH_A only; it does not add elevation head to the closed-loop system head. Surplus pump head is absorbed by the discharge throttling valve per Rule 4.3.
- The 3.40 kW limit is applied directly to computed pump shaft power, as stated in the request.

1. Thermal flow rate
Q = 144.0 kW / (rho*cp*DeltaT) = 144000 / (1200*2000*10.0) = 0.00600 m3/s = 21.60 m3/h.

2. VortaTube pipe selection
A = pi*D^2/4; v = Q/A.

| Model | D (m) | v (m/s) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| VT-32 | 0.032 | 7.46 | fails v <= 3.20 |
| VT-40 | 0.040 | 4.77 | fails v <= 3.20 |
| VT-50 | 0.050 | 3.056 | passes 2.00 <= v <= 3.20 |
| VT-65 | 0.065 | 1.808 | fails v >= 2.00 |

Selected pipe: VT-50. For VT-50, A=0.00196350 m2, v=3.0558 m/s, Re=rho*v*D/mu=1200*3.0558*0.050/0.00240=76,394. This is inside the Blasius range 4000 <= Re <= 100000. f=0.3164/Re^0.25=0.01903.
Dynamic pressure q=0.5*rho*v^2=0.5*1200*3.0558^2=5602.7 Pa=5.6027 kPa.
Suction line: DeltaP_s=(f*L_s/D+K_s)*q=(0.01903*8.0/0.050+2.50)*5.6027=31.07 kPa.
Discharge line: DeltaP_d=(f*L_d/D+K_d)*q=(0.01903*72.0/0.050+11.50)*5.6027=217.97 kPa.
Total pipe drop = 249.04 kPa.

3. FiltraCore duplex filter selection
Filtration requirement: at least 5 um, interpreted as 5 um or finer. Qmax must exceed 21.60 m3/h. Fouled sizing uses Rule 3.2: DeltaP_fouled=2.0*DeltaP_clean.

FC-300 clean drop:
DeltaP_clean = Cf*(mu/mu_ref)*Q + Bf*(rho/rho_ref)*Q^2
= 0.35*(2.40/1.00)*21.60 + 0.015*(1200/1000)*21.60^2
= 18.144 + 8.398 = 26.542 kPa.
DeltaP_fouled = 2.0*26.542 = 53.084 kPa.
FC-300 Qmax=35.0 m3/h >21.60 m3/h. It is a 5 um duplex filter, one basket online and one standby; the fouled condition is one basket at end-of-life.

Screening of alternatives:
- FC-100: 3 um, Qmax=18.0 <21.60, ineligible by flow.
- FC-200: 5 um, Qmax=25.0 >21.60; fouled drop=79.83 kPa. It is flow-eligible but does not leave a feasible pump operating point.
- FC-250: 10 um, coarser than the required 5 um, not eligible.
- FC-300: 5 um, Qmax=35.0 >21.60, fouled drop=53.08 kPa. Selected.

4. VX-Pump and VFD frequency selection
AOR rule: 0.70*Q_BEP(s) <= Q <= 1.20*Q_BEP(s), where Q_BEP(s)=Q_BEP,50*s and s=f_VFD/50.
At Q=21.60 m3/h:
- VX-100: maximum AOR flow at 60 Hz is 1.20*12.0*1.2=17.28 <21.60, so no VX-100 speed is acceptable.
- VX-200: at 50/55/60 Hz, Q_BEP=20.0/22.0/24.0 and AOR bounds are 14.0-24.0, 15.4-26.4, and 16.8-28.8; 21.60 is inside all three.
- VX-300: minimum AOR flow at 50 Hz is 0.70*32.0=22.4 >21.60, so no VX-300 speed is acceptable.
- VX-400: minimum AOR flow at 50 Hz is 0.70*45.0=31.5 >21.60, so no VX-400 speed is acceptable.
Only the VX-200 is AOR-eligible.

VX-200 head: H_pump=H0*s^2 - A_H*Q^2 = 32.50*s^2 - 0.0155*21.60^2 = 32.50*s^2 - 7.2317 m.
System head with FC-300: H_sys=(DeltaP_pipe+DeltaP_load+DeltaP_filter,fouled)/(rho*g) = (249.04+65.0+53.084) kPa / (1200*9.81/1000 kPa/m) = 367.125/11.772 = 31.186 m.

| f_VFD | s | Q_BEP(s) | AOR | H_pump | H_sys | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 50 Hz | 1.00 | 20.0 | 14.0-24.0 | 25.27 m | 31.19 m | fails head |
| 55 Hz | 1.10 | 22.0 | 15.4-26.4 | 32.09 m | 31.19 m | passes head, NPSH, power |
| 60 Hz | 1.20 | 24.0 | 16.8-28.8 | 39.57 m | 31.19 m | fails NPSH and power |

Selected pump: VX-200. Selected VFD frequency: 55 Hz.

5. Cavitation check
NPSH_A=(P_tank-P_v-DeltaP_suction)/(rho*g/1000)-h_s
=(95.0-22.0-31.07)/11.772-0.50
=3.562-0.50=3.062 m.
Pump inlet absolute pressure is 95.0-5.886-31.07=58.05 kPa abs, above Pv=22.0 kPa abs.
At 55 Hz: NPSH_R=N0*s^1.5+A_N*Q^2=1.35*1.10^1.5+0.0018*21.60^2=1.557+0.840=2.397 m.
Required margin: 1.20*NPSH_R=2.877 m. NPSH_A=3.062 m >2.877 m, so the margin is satisfied with ratio 1.278.
At 60 Hz: 1.20*NPSH_R=3.137 m >3.062 m, so 60 Hz is rejected.

6. Viscosity correction and shaft power
Q/Q_BEP(55 Hz)=21.60/22.0=0.9818.
eta_w=eta_max-k_eta*(Q/Q_BEP-1)^2=0.760-0.50*(0.9818-1)^2=0.7598.
C_mu=1-0.05*(mu/1.00-1)=1-0.05*(2.40-1)=0.930.
eta_p=C_mu*eta_w=0.930*0.7598=0.7066.
Hydraulic power=rho*g*Q*H_pump/1000=1200*9.81*0.00600*32.093/1000=2.267 kW.
P_shaft=2.267/0.7066=3.208 kW.
P_shaft=3.208 kW <=3.40 kW drive rating, so the power limit is satisfied. The surplus head H_pump-H_sys=32.093-31.186=0.907 m is absorbed by the discharge throttling valve per Rule 4.3.

7. Other rule checks
- Velocity window: v=3.056 m/s, within 2.00-3.20 m/s.
- Reynolds range: Re=76,394, within 4000-100,000; Blasius friction factor is valid.
- AOR: Q=21.60 m3/h, Q_BEP(55 Hz)=22.0 m3/h, ratio=0.982, inside 0.70-1.20.
- Fouled filter: FC-300 Qmax=35.0 >21.60 m3/h; DeltaP_fouled=53.08 kPa included in system head.
- Viscosity correction: C_mu=0.930 applied to pump efficiency; filter laminar term also corrected by mu/mu_ref=2.40.
- NPSH margin: NPSH_A=3.062 m >=1.20*NPSH_R=2.877 m.
- Pump head: H_pump=32.09 m >=H_sys=31.19 m.
- Pipe maximum working pressure: VT-50 MWP=850 kPa. Maximum shutoff discharge pressure at 55 Hz is approximately P_tank+rho*g*H0*s^2/1000=95.0+11.772*39.325=557.9 kPa abs, below 850 kPa.

8. Skid layout and component set
- Base frame with drip tray, drain, and leak detection; all wetted metallic parts 316L stainless steel; fluoropolymer piping; EPDM/FFKM seals compatible with KryoSol-45; grounding and bonding to control electrostatic charge.
- N2-blanketed expansion tank at 95.0 kPa abs with relief valve, level transmitter, fill/drain, and pressure gauge.
- Suction: VT-50, 8.0 m long, K_s=2.50, with isolation valve, pressure gauge, and temperature sensor to the VX-200 pump inlet.
- Pump: VX-200 centrifugal pump driven by the 3.40 kW VFD set to 55 Hz, with discharge check valve and pressure gauge.
- Discharge: duplex FiltraCore FC-300, 5 um, one basket online and one standby, with differential-pressure transmitter and changeover valve; flow meter; 72.0 m VT-50 return line with K_d=11.50; cold plate; return to expansion tank.
- Controls/interlocks: VFD frequency fixed at 55 Hz; trip/alarm on high filter differential pressure, low NPSH margin, low flow, high temperature, and leak detection.

Results

|---|---:|
| selected_pipe (-) | VT-50 |
| selected_filter (-) | FC-300 |
| selected_pump (-) | VX-200 |
| vfd_frequency_Hz (Hz) | 55 |

question: T4-16
answer:
Process Engineer selection per Kaelen-Vortec Application Standard KV-AS-112.

1. Common pipe and system calculations at Q = 90.0 m3/h = 0.0250 m3/s

Pipe area: A = π/4 (0.1023)^2 = 8.2194e-3 m2
Pipe velocity: v = Q/A = 0.0250/8.2194e-3 = 3.0416 m/s
Velocity head: hv = v^2/(2g) = 3.0416^2/(2*9.81) = 0.4715 m
Reynolds number: Re = v D_pipe/ν = 3.0416*0.1023/(1.2e-6) = 2.593e5
Relative roughness: ε/D = 0.045/102.3 = 4.399e-4
Colebrook: 1/sqrt(f) = -2 log10[ε/(3.7D) + 2.51/(Re sqrt(f))] gives f_Darcy = 0.01807.

System head:
H_sys = Δz_total + (p_reactor - p_atm)/(ρg) + f (L_total/D) hv + ΣK_total hv
= 22.0 + 83700/(1150*9.81) + 0.01807*(85.0/0.1023)*0.4715 + 14.0*0.4715
= 22.0 + 7.419 + 7.081 + 6.601
= 43.101 m.

NPSH_A at the pump suction flange, with the pump centerline z_s = 3.20 m above the supply-tank liquid surface:
NPSH_A = (p_atm - p_v)/(ρg) - z_s - [f (L_s/D) + ΣK_s] hv
= 83300/(1150*9.81) - 3.20 - [0.01807*(6.0/0.1023) + 2.8]*0.4715
= 7.384 - 3.20 - 1.820
= 2.364 m.

2. Candidate screening using KV-AS-112

For each model and integer D_trim in [0.85D0, D0]:
H_pump(Q,D) = H0 (D/D0)^2 - S0 Q^2
Q_BEP,trim = Q_BEP0 (D/D0); POR requires 0.70 Q_BEP,trim ≤ 90 ≤ 1.15 Q_BEP,trim
NPSH_R,corr = NPSH_R0 (D0/D)^1.5; cavitation requires NPSH_A ≥ 1.15 NPSH_R,corr + 0.50 m
η_pump = η_max - k_η (90 - Q_BEP,trim)^2 - 0.25(1 - D/D0)
P_shaft = ρ g Q H_pump / η_pump; motor rule requires P_shaft ≤ P_motor,derated = 0.88 P_motor,nameplate

Screening results:
| Model | Head-limited D (mm) | POR-limited D (mm) | NPSH-limited D (mm) | Governing D_min (mm) | Outcome |
| KV-100-200 | none: H at D0 = 38.81 m < 43.10 m | - | - | - | fail head |
| KV-80-250 | 228 | 231 | 236 | 236 | P_shaft at 236 mm = 18.62 kW > 16.28 kW derated; fail motor |
| KV-100-250 | 228 | ≤228 | ≤228 | 228 | pass; P_shaft = 16.18 kW |
| KV-125-250 | 219 | ≤219 | ≤219 | 219 | pass; P_shaft = 17.16 kW |

Both KV-100-250 and KV-125-250 pass. KV-100-250 has the lower shaft power, so it is selected.

3. Selected pump check: KV-100-250, D_trim = 228 mm

Trim range: 0.85 D0 = 0.85*250 = 212.5 mm, so the minimum integer trim is 213 mm; D_trim = 228 mm is within range.
H_pump = 62*(228/250)^2 - 0.00100*90^2 = 43.468 m > H_sys = 43.101 m.
Check of next smaller trim: D = 227 mm gives H_pump = 62*(227/250)^2 - 8.10 = 43.017 m < 43.101 m, so 228 mm is the minimum acceptable integer trim.
Q_BEP,trim = 100*(228/250) = 91.2 m3/h; POR = [0.70*91.2, 1.15*91.2] = [63.84, 104.88] m3/h, which contains Q = 90 m3/h.
NPSH_R,corr = 1.25*(250/228)^1.5 = 1.435 m.
Required NPSH_A = 1.15*1.435 + 0.50 = 2.150 m; actual NPSH_A = 2.364 m, so cavitation rule passes.
η_pump = 0.780 - 0.00010*(90 - 91.2)^2 - 0.25*(1 - 228/250) = 0.75786.
P_shaft = 1150*9.81*0.0250*43.468/0.75786 = 16.18 kW.
P_motor,derated = 0.88*22.0 = 19.36 kW; P_shaft = 16.18 kW ≤ 19.36 kW, so motor rule passes.

question: T4-21
answer:
Selection basis and assumptions
- Candidate set: the five single-stage KGD models listed in Pub. KD-2024-09.
- Application shock factor: Ka = 1.15 for electric servo, cyclic indexing duty.
- Ambient 40 C: C_th = 0.82.
- Cycle time is 1.00 s = 60 cycles/min, which is greater than 30 cycles/min, so C_duty = 0.90.
- Dwell is 0.20 s / 1.00 s = 20% <= 25%, so dwell is excluded from the T_rms denominator per catalogue rule.
- Bearing speed n_m is averaged over the full cycle including dwell.
- Radial load is constant 2400 N at x = 45 mm from the shaft shoulder.
- Peak motor torque is checked as absolute magnitude, including the deceleration phase.
- Load inertia at the gearhead output is included in T_out; motor rotor inertia and gearhead input inertia J_g are included in the motor-side inertia term.

Kinematics and output-torque profile
- Output speed at indexing: 150 rpm = 15.70796 rad/s.
- Acceleration magnitude: alpha = 15.70796 / 0.20 = 78.53982 rad/s^2.
- Load inertia torque: J_L * alpha = 0.450 * 78.53982 = 35.3429 N·m.
- Phase 1 acceleration: T_out = 45 + 35.3429 = 80.3429 N·m.
- Phase 2 constant speed: T_out = 85.0000 N·m.
- Phase 3 deceleration: T_drive + T_friction = J_L * alpha, with T_friction = -45 N·m and alpha = -78.53982 rad/s^2. Therefore T_drive = -35.3429 - (-45) = +9.6571 N·m. The friction over-assists deceleration, so the drive must hold a small positive torque.
- Phase 4 dwell: T_out = 0.
- Peak output torque: T_peak = max(80.3429, 85.0000, 9.6571) = 85.0000 N·m.
- RMS output torque over active motion phases:
  T_rms = sqrt((80.3429^2 * 0.20 + 85^2 * 0.40 + 9.6571^2 * 0.20) / (0.20 + 0.40 + 0.20))
  T_rms = sqrt(4199.649 / 0.80) = 72.454 N·m.

Model screening

| KGD-75-08 | 4.2 | 75*0.82*0.90 = 55.35 | Fail: 72.45 > 55.35 | Pass: 85 <= 200/1.15 = 173.9 | 3161.9 | Fail: 3161.9 > 2500 | ~5040 | 15.11 | Reject: thermal and radial |
| KGD-90-08 | 6.8 | 92*0.82*0.90 = 67.90 | Fail: 72.45 > 67.90 | Pass: 85 <= 300/1.15 = 260.9 | 2880.0 | Pass: 2880 <= 3600 | 23710 | 16.18 | Reject: thermal |
| KGD-90-10 | 7.0 | 105*0.82*0.90 = 77.49 | Pass: 72.45 <= 77.49 | Pass: 85 <= 330/1.15 = 287.0 | 2880.0 | Pass: 2880 <= 3600 | 23710 | 15.11 | Select: lightest passing model |
| KGD-115-05 | 11.2 | 140*0.82*0.90 = 103.32 | Pass: 72.45 <= 103.32 | Pass: 85 <= 450/1.15 = 391.3 | 2666.7 | Pass: 2666.7 <= 5200 | ~112970 | 18.84 | Reject: motor peak 18.84 > 18.0 |
| KGD-115-08 | 11.5 | 175*0.82*0.90 = 129.15 | Pass: 72.45 <= 129.15 | Pass: 85 <= 520/1.15 = 452.2 | 2666.7 | Pass: 2666.7 <= 5200 | ~112970 | 16.56 | Pass, but heavier than KGD-90-10 |

Selected model verification: KGD-90-10
- Ratio i = 10; mass = 7.0 kg; T_N = 105 N·m; T_max = 330 N·m; n_1,max = 4500 rpm; J_g = 0.00798 kg·m^2; eta = 0.96.
- Peak output check: 85.00 <= 330 / 1.15 = 286.96 N·m. Pass.
- Thermal check: T_th,derated = 105 * 0.82 * 0.90 = 77.49 N·m. T_rms = 72.45 N·m <= 77.49 N·m. Pass, margin 5.04 N·m.
- Radial load: Frame 90 has A = 45 mm, L_ref = 30 mm, F_r,max = 3600 N. F_r,eq = 2400 * (45 + 45) / (45 + 30) = 2400 * 90 / 75 = 2880 N <= 3600 N. Pass.
- Bearing speed: n_m = (75*0.20 + 150*0.40 + 75*0.20 + 0*0.20) / 1.00 = 90 rpm.
- Bearing life: L10h = (10^6 / (60 * 90)) * (14200 / (2880 * 1.15))^(10/3) = 185.185 * (14200 / 3312)^(10/3) = 185.185 * 4.28744^3.3333 = 23710 h. Pass, 23710 >= 15000 h.
- Motor torque during acceleration: T_m = 80.3429 / (10 * 0.96) + (0.00060 + 0.00798) * 10 * 78.53982 = 8.3691 + 6.7387 = 15.1078 N·m.
- Motor torque during constant speed: T_m = 85 / (10 * 0.96) = 8.8542 N·m.
- Motor torque during deceleration: T_m = 9.6571 / (10 * 0.96) + (0.00060 + 0.00798) * 10 * (-78.53982) = 1.0059 - 6.7387 = -5.7328 N·m; absolute magnitude 5.73 N·m.
- Peak motor torque = 15.11 N·m <= 18.0 N·m. Pass.
- Input speed: 150 rpm * 10 = 1500 rpm <= 4500 rpm. Pass.

Conclusion: The lightest KGD-Series gearhead that satisfies all catalogue peak-torque, thermal, radial-load, bearing-life, motor-torque, and input-speed limits is KGD-90-10. The lighter KGD-90-08 is rejected by the derated thermal torque limit, and KGD-115-05 is rejected by the 18.0 N·m peak motor-torque limit.

SELECTION AND SIZING

Sizing is per Vexor VES-14 Rev. 4.2. Fluid is liquid methanol: rho = 790 kg/m3, Gf = 790/1000 = 0.79, Pv = 32.0 kPa abs, Pc = 8096 kPa abs, nu = 0.70 cSt at 38 C. Because nu < 20 cSt, the baseline Newtonian liquid equation applies with FR = 1.

Critical pressure ratio factor:
FF = 0.96 - 0.28*sqrt(Pv/Pc)
   = 0.96 - 0.28*sqrt(32.0/8096)
   = 0.94240

At maximum flow: P1 = 1600 kPa abs, P2 = 750 kPa abs, dP = 850 kPa = 8.50 bar, Q = 145 m3/h.
dP/P1 = 850/1600 = 0.53125 > 0.50, so the -M stage-interaction factor Km is active at max flow.
Cv0,max = Q / (0.865*sqrt(dP_bar/Gf))
         = 145 / (0.865*sqrt(8.50/0.79))
         = 51.104

At minimum flow: P1 = 1800 kPa abs, P2 = 1100 kPa abs, dP = 700 kPa = 7.00 bar, Q = 5.0 m3/h.
dP/P1 = 700/1800 = 0.38889 <= 0.50, so Km = 1.000 at min flow for all trims.
Cv0,min = 5.0 / (0.865*sqrt(7.00/0.79))
         = 1.9419

INCPIENT CAVITATION SCREENING AT MAXIMUM FLOW

The allowable incipient pressure drop is:
dP_ic = Fkc * Fp^2 * (P1 - FF*Pv)
with P1 - FF*Pv = 1600 - 0.94240*32.0 = 1569.843 kPa.

The required max-flow Cv is:
Cv,req = Cv0,max / (Fp*Km)

SELECTION: Thermovance TVC-250-AL (Al 6061-T6), 1.85 kg — the lightest TVC-Series plate that simultaneously satisfies the 95.0 °C baseplate limit, the 38.0 kPa corrected pressure-drop budget, and the aluminium erosion-corrosion velocity limit at 6.00 L/min of 50/50 EG-water.

=== 1. INPUTS (as given) ===
P_mod = 650 W each, P_total = 1300 W; footprint 60 mm x 60 mm = 36.0 cm2 per module; T_in = 45.0 °C; Q = 6.00 L/min; coolant 50/50 EG-water: rho = 1055 kg/m3, cp = 3450 J/(kg·K), mu = 0.00210 Pa·s; TIM R'' = 0.120 K·cm2/W; limits: T_b <= 95.0 °C, dP_total <= 38.0 kPa, v_ch <= 2.20 m/s (Al) / 3.50 m/s (Cu).

Derived coolant properties (evaluated at the 45.0 °C inlet — conservative, since viscosity falls as the fluid warms toward 48.6 °C):
  nu = mu/rho = 0.00210/1055 = 1.99052e-6 m2/s
  (nu/nu_ref)^0.25 = (1.99052e-6/0.890e-6)^0.25 = (2.23654)^0.25 = 1.22291
  rho/rho_ref = 1055/997 = 1.05818
  rho/1000 = 1.055

Flow conversions:
  Qv = 6.00 L/min = 1.000e-4 m3/s
  mdot = rho·Qv = 1055 x 1.000e-4 = 0.10550 kg/s

=== 2. METHOD (TAN-08, Flow Topology S) ===
Channel velocity:  v_ch = Qv / (N_ch · A_ch)
Pressure drop:    dP_core = K_hyd · (rho/rho_ref) · (nu/nu_ref)^0.25 · Q^1.75 = 29.765 · K_hyd   [kPa]
                  dP_port = K_port · (rho/1000) · Q^2 = 37.980 · K_port                             [kPa]
                  dP_total = dP_core + dP_port   (includes manifolds + Reynolds/viscosity correction)
Outlet temp:      T_out = T_in + P_total/(mdot·cp) = 45.0 + 1300/(0.10550 x 3450) = 45.0 + 3.572 = 48.572 °C
TIM:              R_tim = R''/A_mod = 0.120/36.0 = 0.003333 K/W per module
Constriction:     Ms = (W_f/60)^0.35  ->  1.15247 (W_f=90 mm),  1.08123 (W_f=75 mm)
Convective:       R_conv = R_th,cat · Ms · F_gly,  F_gly = 1.28 (50/50 EG-water)
Peak baseplate:   T_b,max = T_out + P_mod·(R_tim + R_conv)   (Module 2, referenced to outlet)
Module 1 check:   T_b,1 = (T_in + P_mod/(mdot·cp)) + P_mod·(R_tim + R_conv) = 46.786 + 650·(R_tim+R_conv)

=== 3. SCREENING — ALL FIVE CATALOGUE MODELS ===

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TVC-180-AL | 1.15 | 2.381 | 2.20 FAIL | 36.91 | 4.37 | 41.28 | FAIL | 1.15247 | 0.073758 | 98.68 | FAIL | Rejected (velocity + dP + thermal) |
| TVC-200-AL | 1.45 | 1.852 | OK | 29.17 | 3.72 | 32.89 | OK | 1.15247 | 0.071545 | 97.24 | FAIL | Rejected (thermal) |
| TVC-250-AL | 1.85 | 1.562 | OK | 31.85 | 3.80 | 35.65 | OK | 1.08123 | 0.062417 | 91.31 | OK | **SELECTED** |
| TVC-220-CU | 2.60 | 2.083 | OK | 35.72 | 4.18 | 39.90 | FAIL | 1.08123 | 0.054667 | 86.27 | OK | Rejected (dP) |
| TVC-260-CU | 3.10 | 1.667 | OK | 27.98 | 3.61 | 31.59 | OK | 1.08123 | 0.052591 | 84.92 | OK | Compliant, but 1.25 kg heavier |

Worked arithmetic for the selected plate (TVC-250-AL: N_ch=16, A_ch=4.00 mm2, W_f=75.0 mm, R_th,cat=0.0451 K/W, K_hyd=1.070, K_port=0.100):
  v_ch = 1.000e-4 / (16 x 4.00e-6) = 1.5625 m/s  ->  (2.20 - 1.5625)/2.20 = 29.0% below the Al erosion-corrosion limit
  dP_core = 1.070 x 29.765 = 31.848 kPa;  dP_port = 0.100 x 37.980 = 3.798 kPa;  dP_total = 35.646 kPa
  Ms = (75/60)^0.35 = 1.08123;  R_conv = 0.0451 x 1.08123 x 1.28 = 0.062417 K/W
  T_b,max = 48.572 + 650 x (0.003333 + 0.062417) = 48.572 + 42.738 = 91.31 °C
  T_b,1 (Module 1, conservative) = 46.786 + 42.738 = 89.52 °C

=== 4. WHY THE LIGHTER ALUMINIUM PLATES LOSE ===
- TVC-180-AL (1.15 kg) is the lightest plate in the catalogue but its 14 x 3.00 mm2 channel set gives 2.381 m/s (> 2.20 m/s Al limit) and 41.28 kPa (> 38.0 kPa), and it is thermally short at 98.68 °C. It fails three constraints.
- TVC-200-AL (1.45 kg) passes velocity (1.852 m/s) and pressure (32.89 kPa) but its 90 mm active fin width combined with 60 mm modules gives Ms = 1.1525, driving R_conv to 0.07155 K/W and T_b,max to 97.24 °C — 2.2 K over the 95.0 °C limit. It is NOT selectable; choosing it would be a thermal-constraint violation.
- TVC-220-CU (2.60 kg) is thermally comfortable (86.27 °C) but its K_hyd = 1.200 gives 39.90 kPa, exceeding the 38.0 kPa pump-loop budget by 5.0%. Rejected on hydraulics.
- TVC-260-CU (3.10 kg) is the most capable plate (31.59 kPa, 84.92 °C) but is 1.25 kg heavier than the selected aluminium plate. Kept as the fallback if the thermal margin is later consumed (see §6).

=== 5. MARGINS ON THE SELECTED PLATE ===
- Velocity: 1.5625 vs 2.20 m/s -> 0.638 m/s margin (29.0%).
- Pressure drop: 35.65 vs 38.0 kPa -> 2.35 kPa margin (6.2%).
- Baseplate: 91.31 vs 95.0 °C -> 3.69 K margin (7.3% of the 50 K rise above inlet).
- Outlet: 48.57 °C; baseplate-to-coolant delta 42.7 K; TIM contributes 2.17 K of that (650 x 0.003333).

=== 6. ASSUMPTIONS, SENSITIVITIES AND VERIFICATION ACTIONS ===
1. 'Side-by-side' interpretation: the TVC catalogue defines the dual-module envelope only as two modules in tandem along the flow axis (Flow Topology S, series-serpentine), which is what the TAN-08 Module-2 formula assumes. If the modules are instead mounted abreast transverse to flow (parallel over the same fin length), the Module-2/outlet referencing no longer applies: both modules would see roughly the mean coolant temperature, and the per-module resistance would be re-derived. VERIFY the mechanical mounting arrangement against the plate's module-land pattern before release; the hydraulic and velocity conclusions are unaffected, the thermal conclusion is.
2. Viscosity reference temperature: evaluated at the 45.0 °C inlet, which is conservative — at the 48.6 °C mean/outlet the viscosity is lower and dP would be lower still. The 6.2% dP margin therefore holds on the pessimistic side.
3. Thermal margin is the tightest relative risk (3.7 K). Sensitivity: the 1.85 kg plate can absorb roughly +56 W per module (or +0.006 K/W of R_conv) before breaching 95.0 °C. If the phase-change TIM is re-specified worse than 0.120 K·cm2/W, or if module loss rises above ~706 W each, move to TVC-260-CU (3.10 kg) which buys 6.4 K.
4. Both modules individually satisfy the limit under the catalogue's conservative outlet-referenced rule (Module 2 = 91.31 °C; Module 1 <= 89.52 °C).
5. Sealed avionics bay: the liquid loop is sealed, so altitude does not change the hydraulic numbers, but the plate must be pressure-tested to at least 2x the 38 kPa operating drop plus pump head, and the aluminium plate requires inhibited 50/50 EG-water (silicate-free, e.g. ASTM D3306) to preserve the 2.20 m/s erosion-corrosion allowance. Specify the plate with a conductive, non-outgassing finish and confirm pump NPSH at the highest cabin altitude; neither changes the model choice.
6. Mass is treated as the sole selection criterion per the request; no envelope, cost, or availability data were supplied.

=== 7. RESULT ===
Install the Thermovance TVC-250-AL (Al 6061-T6, 1.85 kg) with both 60 mm x 60 mm SiC modules on 0.120 K·cm2/W phase-change TIM, 6.00 L/min of 50/50 EG-water at 45.0 °C inlet. Expected peak baseplate temperature 91.3 °C, corrected assembly pressure drop 35.6 kPa, channel velocity 1.56 m/s.

| TVC-250-AL | 1.85 | 1.56 | 35.6 | 48.6 | 91.3 |

# Lowest-Cost Astradyne EPC-Series DC-Link Bank
## 150 kW three-phase active rectifier - 12 000 m unpressurized fairing, 65.0 °C ambient

### 1. Design inputs used

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Nominal DC bus | V_DC,nom | 900 V |
| Repetitive switching overshoot | dV_overshoot | 135 V |
| Peak repetitive operating voltage | V_pk | 1035 V |
| Low-frequency ripple component | I_1.2k | 90.0 A_rms @ 1.20 kHz |
| Carrier ripple component | I_40k | 140.0 A_rms @ 40.0 kHz |
| Minimum bank capacitance | C_min | 220 µF |
| Carrier ripple limit | dV_pp,max | 12.0 V pk-pk @ 40.0 kHz |
| Altitude | H | 12 000 m |
| Local ambient | T_amb | 65.0 °C |
| Max dielectric hot-spot | T_max | 105.0 °C |
| Topology | - | all capacitors in parallel, identical units (required by AAM-12 §3.1 per-unit formulas) |

All calculations below use the AAM-12 Rev. 3.0 tabulated values directly: C_alt,V from §2.1, M_alt,th = 1.620 at 12 000 m from Table 3, K_f = 0.7143 (1.20 kHz) and 0.8333 (40.0 kHz) from Table 2, and the catalogue nominal capacitances with no tolerance/aging derating (sensitivity checked in §7).

### 2. Altitude / voltage screening (kills the 1100 V model)

C_alt,V = 1.000 - 0.015 · (12 000 - 3 000)/1 000 = 1.000 - 0.135 = **0.865**

| Model | V_NDC (V) | V_w,derated = V_NDC · 0.865 (V) | vs. V_pk = 1035 V | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| EPC-1100-80 | 1100 | 951.50 | short by 83.50 V | **ELIMINATED at any N** |
| EPC-1200-60 | 1200 | 1038.00 | +3.00 V margin | eligible |
| EPC-1250-80 | 1250 | 1081.25 | +46.25 V margin | eligible |

The corona derating is a per-capacitor voltage limit, so no parallel count can rescue EPC-1100-80. The trade is EPC-1200-60 vs. EPC-1250-80.

### 3. Frequency-weighted effective ripple current

I_eff,total = sqrt[ (90.0 / 0.7143)^2 + (140.0 / 0.8333)^2 ]
           = sqrt[ (126.0)^2 + (168.0)^2 ]
           = sqrt[ 15 876 + 28 224 ] = sqrt[ 44 100 ] = **210.0 A_rms**

Per capacitor in a bank of N: I_eff,unit = 210.0 / N  (A_rms, referred to 10 kHz).

### 4. Compliance sweep - every eligible model and count

Equations applied:

- I_eff,unit = 210.0 / N
- P_loss = I_eff,unit^2 · ESR_10kHz
- R_th,eff = R_th,ca · 1.620
- T_core = 65.0 + P_loss · R_th,eff   (limit 105.0 °C)
- ESR(40 kHz) = ESR_10kHz / (0.8333)^2 = 1.44 · ESR_10kHz
- dV_pp = sqrt(3)·140 / (4 · 40 000 · C_total) + 2·sqrt(3)·140 · ESR(40 kHz) / N   (limit 12.0 V)
  - capacitive term constant: sqrt(3)·140 = 242.487 A
  - ESR term constant: 2·sqrt(3)·140 = 484.974 A

| Model | N | C_total (µF) | Cost (USD) | I_eff/unit (A_rms) | T_core (°C) | dV_pp @40 kHz (V) | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| EPC-1100-80 | 3 | 240 | 420 | 70.0 | 114.22 | 6.63 | FAIL - voltage (951.5 < 1035) and hot-spot |
| EPC-1100-80 | 4 | 320 | 560 | 52.5 | 92.68 | 5.01 | FAIL - voltage (951.5 < 1035) |
| EPC-1200-60 | 4 | 240 | 520 | 52.5 | 110.69 | 6.63 | FAIL - hot-spot (110.69 > 105.0) |
| **EPC-1200-60** | **5** | **300** | **650** | **42.0** | **94.24** | **5.30** | **PASS - lowest cost** |
| EPC-1200-60 | 6 | 360 | 780 | 35.0 | 85.31 | 4.42 | pass, costlier |
| EPC-1250-80 | 3 | 240 | 555 | 70.0 | 111.94 | 6.63 | FAIL - hot-spot (111.94 > 105.0) |
| EPC-1250-80 | 4 | 320 | 740 | 52.5 | 91.40 | 4.97 | pass, costlier |
| EPC-1250-80 | 5 | 400 | 925 | 42.0 | 81.90 | 3.98 | pass, costlier |

Worked arithmetic for the two binding cases:

- **EPC-1200-60, N = 4:** P_loss = 52.5^2 · 0.0018 = 4.9613 W; R_th,eff = 5.685 · 1.620 = 9.2097 K/W; ΔT = 45.69 K → T_core = 110.69 °C. **Fails by 5.69 K**, so N = 4 is not usable even though it meets 240 µF and 6.63 V ripple.
- **EPC-1250-80, N = 3:** P_loss = 70.0^2 · 0.00135 = 6.615 W; R_th,eff = 4.38 · 1.620 = 7.0956 K/W; ΔT = 46.94 K → T_core = 111.94 °C. **Fails by 6.94 K.**
- **EPC-1200-60, N = 5:** P_loss = 42.0^2 · 0.0018 = 3.1752 W; ΔT = 3.1752 · 9.2097 = 29.24 K → T_core = 94.24 °C. Pass.

In every model the **thermal hot-spot constraint, not the ripple limit and not the capacitance minimum, sets the minimum count**: at the count where ripple and capacitance are already satisfied, the core is 5-7 K over the 105 °C limit.

### 5. Cost comparison and selection

| Model | Minimum compliant N | Minimum compliant cost (USD) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| EPC-1100-80 | none (voltage-infeasible at 12 000 m) | - |
| **EPC-1200-60** | **5** | **650** |
| EPC-1250-80 | 4 | 740 |

**Selected bank: 5 × EPC-1200-60 in parallel = 300 µF, 650 USD.** The EPC-1250-80's lower ESR and lower R_th buy it a count of 4 instead of 5, but 4 × 185 = 740 USD > 5 × 130 = 650 USD, so the cheaper unit wins the cost trade.

### 6. Compliance verification of the selected bank (5 × EPC-1200-60)

| Constraint family | Requirement | Achieved | Margin | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Capacitance (§3, ask 3) | >= 220 µF | 5 × 60 = 300.0 µF | +80.0 µF (+36 %) | PASS |
| Voltage / altitude (§2) | V_pk <= 1038.0 V | 1035 V | +3.0 V (0.29 %) | PASS (thin - see §7) |
| Frequency weighting (§3.1) | K_f from Table 2 | both harmonics at tabulated points (1.20 kHz, 40.0 kHz); no interpolation or extrapolation | - | PASS |
| Ripple current per unit (§3.1) | I_eff,unit <= altitude-derated 10 kHz rating | 42.0 A_rms vs. 62.5 / sqrt(1.620) = 49.11 A_rms | +7.11 A_rms | PASS |
| Thermal hot-spot (§3.3) | T_core <= 105.0 °C | 94.24 °C | 10.76 K | PASS |
| Carrier ripple (§4) | dV_pp <= 12.0 V | 5.30 V | 6.70 V | PASS |

Ripple voltage detail (N = 5, C_total = 300 µF, ESR(40 kHz) = 1.80 · 1.44 = 2.592 mΩ):

- Capacitive term = 242.487 / (4 · 40 000 · 300e-6) = 242.487 / 48.0 = 5.0518 V
- ESR term = 484.974 · 0.002592 / 5 = 1.25705 / 5 = 0.2514 V
- **dV_pp = 5.0518 + 0.2514 = 5.30 V pk-pk** (the capacitive term dominates 20:1, which is why the count is thermally rather than ripple-driven)

Thermal detail: P_loss = 42.0^2 · 1.80 mΩ = 3.1752 W per unit; R_th,eff = 5.685 · 1.620 = 9.2097 K/W; ΔT = 29.24 K; T_core = 65.0 + 29.24 = **94.24 °C**. Total bank dissipation = 5 × 3.1752 = 15.88 W.

### 7. Design notes and sensitivities the reviewer should see

1. **Voltage margin is 3.0 V (0.29 %).** Any increase of the repetitive overshoot above 138 V, or any reduction in the altitude factor below 0.8625, invalidates EPC-1200-60 and flips the answer to 4 × EPC-1250-80 (740 USD, 46.25 V margin). Confirm the 135 V overshoot with the measured busbar/stray-inductance di/dt before releasing the BOM; if the overshoot figure is not firm, the 1250 V model is the risk-appropriate choice at +90 USD.
2. **Capacitance tolerance/aging:** the selection is robust. With a 10 % end-of-life/tolerance derating, 5 × 60 × 0.9 = 270 µF still exceeds 220 µF, so no count change is needed (EPC-1250-80 would need 4 units either way at 740 USD).
3. **Ripple sharing:** the 42.0 A_rms figure assumes an equal split. With ±10 % busbar-imbalance the worst unit sees 46.2 A_rms → T_core = 100.4 °C, still compliant but the margin drops to 4.6 K. Layout requirement: laminated symmetric busbar, equal-length straps to each can, capacitors in a single row with the DC feed at the row centre.
4. **Ambient headroom:** at the selected 42.0 A_rms per unit the hot-spot limit is reached at T_amb = 75.76 °C, so the 65.0 °C local ambient assumption must hold at the capacitor row (not just at the fairing wall); local preheat from the IGBT heatsink must be verified.

Duty: vertical hoist; suspended mass m = 800 kg; hoisting speed v = 0.25 m/s; drum pitch radius r = 0.20 m; ramp time t_r = 0.25 s; g = 9.81 m/s².

Assumptions: rope tension equals the suspended weight plus the inertial force during the ramp; the rope acts at the pitch radius r = 0.20 m (single-layer winding, constant radius); drum, bearing, gearbox and rope losses are neglected because no values are given; no service factor or duty-cycle derating is supplied in the WR catalogue, so catalogue limits are treated as absolute. a = v / t_r = 0.25 / 0.25 = 1.00 m/s².

Peak rope force at the end of the ramp: F_pk = m(g + a) = 800 × (9.81 + 1.00) = 8648 N.

T_pk = F_pk r = 8648 × 0.20 = 1729.6 N·m.

n = ω × 60 / (2π) = 1.25 × 9.5493 = 11.94 rpm.
The maximum speed demand is 11.94 rpm.

4. Output power

P_pk = T_pk ω = 1729.6 × 1.25 = 2162 W.

## Kestrel jacket selection — 120 mm OD horizontal steel pipe, 200 °C surface, 25 °C ambient

### 1. Basis and inputs (all from the request or the Calder catalogue; no other product data used)

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pipe outer radius (OD 120 mm) | r1 | 0.060 m |
| Metal outer surface temperature (held) | Ti | 200 °C |
| Ambient air | Tamb | 25 °C |
| External surface coefficient (convection + radiation combined, constant) | h | 8.0 W/m²·K |
| Driving ΔT | — | 175 K |
| Heat-loss limit | — | ≤ 80 W/m |
| Outer surface limit | — | ≤ 50 °C |
| Radial-build limit | — | ≤ 60 mm |
| Installed-mass limit | — | ≤ 3.0 kg/m |
| Cost basis | — | catalogue supply cost EUR/m (only product data available; installed/labour cost is not in the catalogue and is excluded) |

Steady state, one-dimensional radial conduction; pipe-wall resistance neglected (no steel thickness/conductivity given, and it is ~1 % of the jacket resistance), so the jacket inner surface is at 200 °C.

### 2. Method (per metre of pipe, cylindrical geometry — not a flat-wall approximation)

Thermal resistances in series, per metre (K·m/W):

- Conduction through the jacket:  R_cond = ln(r2/r1) / (2π k)
- External film (convection + radiation, combined):  R_surf = 1 / (2π r2 h)

Then:

- q' = (Ti − Tamb) / (R_cond + R_surf)   [W/m]
- Ts = Tamb + q' · R_surf   [°C]
- k is not constant: the catalogue defines k(T) = k20·(1 + b·(T − 20)), so k is evaluated at the jacket mean temperature Tm = (Ti + Ts)/2 and the three equations are iterated together (q', Ts, k, Tm) until Ts changes by < 0.01 K. Typical convergence in 4–5 passes.

Critical-radius check: k/h ≈ 0.037/8 ≈ 4.6 mm, far below every r2 considered, so added thickness always reduces heat loss here (no critical-radius anomaly).

### 3. Iteration results and constraint screening

| KJ-20 | 20 | 0.080 | 0.05346 | 132.2 | 0.8564 | 0.2487 | **158.4** | **64.4** | pass | pass (1.1) | FAIL | FAIL | 14 |
| KJ-40 | 40 | 0.100 | 0.04883 | 121.8 | 1.6649 | 0.1989 | **93.9** | 43.7 | pass | pass (2.0) | FAIL | pass | 26 |
| KJ-55 | 55 | 0.115 | 0.03668 | 117.6 | 2.8228 | 0.1730 | **58.4** | **35.1** | pass | pass (2.6) | pass | pass | 39 |
| KJ-70 | 70 | 0.130 | 0.04058 | 116.7 | 3.0328 | 0.1530 | 54.9 | 33.4 | **FAIL (70)** | **FAIL (3.4)** | pass | pass | 52 |

- KJ-20 fails on both thermal limits — too thin for 175 K driving ΔT.
- KJ-40 meets the 50 °C touch limit (43.7 °C) but rejects 93.9 W/m, 17 % over the 80 W/m cap. Rejected.
- KJ-70 has the lowest heat loss and surface temperature but its 70 mm radial build exceeds the 60 mm limit and its 3.4 kg/m exceeds the 3.0 kg/m limit. Excluded on both hard constraints. Note it is also the most expensive (52 EUR/m), so the exclusion does not change the selection — the answer is robust to whether those two limits are treated as hard or soft.
- KJ-55 is the only jacket that satisfies all four limits simultaneously, hence it is the lowest-cost compliant jacket (39 EUR/m).

### 4. Verification of the selected jacket (KJ-55)

- Conduction side: q' = 2π k (Ti − Ts)/ln(r2/r1) = 2π × 0.03668 × 164.9 / 0.65059 = **58.4 W/m**
- Surface side: q' = 2π r2 h (Ts − Tamb) = 2π × 0.115 × 8.0 × 10.1 = **58.4 W/m**  → energy balance closes.
- Margins: heat loss 58.4 vs 80 W/m (27 % margin); surface 35.1 vs 50 °C (14.9 K margin); build 55 vs 60 mm (5 mm margin); mass 2.6 vs 3.0 kg/m (0.4 kg/m margin).
- Thermal resistance split: jacket 2.823 of 2.996 K·m/W total (94 %); external film 0.173 K·m/W (6 %).

### 5. Sensitivity the reader must know about (does not change the answer as specified)

If k were taken as the 20 °C catalogue value with no temperature correction, the numbers would be: KJ-20 125.6 W/m / 56.2 °C; KJ-40 71.2 W/m / 39.2 °C; KJ-55 51.3 W/m / 33.9 °C; KJ-70 46.4 W/m / 32.1 °C. On that basis KJ-40 would pass and would win at 26 EUR/m. That basis is rejected here because the catalogue itself supplies the b coefficient and defines k(T) = k20·(1 + b·(T − 20)); evaluating at the mean temperature is the standard treatment (ISO 12241 / ASTM C680 practice) and the constant-k20 route understates the mean conductivity of KJ-40 by 36 % (0.036 → 0.0488 W/m·K), i.e. it is non-conservative against the 80 W/m duty. Recommendation: KJ-55.

Sensitivity to h: at h = 10 W/m²·K (high-emissivity surface) KJ-55 would give ≈ 61.9 W/m and 33.5 °C — still compliant; at h = 6 W/m²·K ≈ 54.4 W/m and 37.2 °C — still compliant. The selection is not marginal to the stated coefficient.

**Kinematics.** Move angle θ = 90° = π/2 = 1.5708 rad; move time T = 0.40 s; symmetric triangular speed profile with t_acc = t_dec = 0.20 s. # Cable selection — Harton Vanta single-core copper, 180 A, 400 V L-L, 40 m, cosφ = 0.85 lagging

## 1. Basis of calculation

| Quantity | Value | Source / note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Load current I | 180 A | given |
| System voltage U | 400 V line-to-line | given |
| Voltage-drop limit | 3 % of 400 V = **12.0 V** (line-to-line) | constraint 1; √3 convention per three-phase drop formula |
| Route length L | 40 m = 0.040 km (one-way) | given |
| Power factor | cosφ = 0.85, sinφ = 0.5268 | given |
| Ambient / installation | free air, 40 °C, trefoil | catalogue sheet — ampacity used as published, no further derating factor supplied |
| R, X | per conductor at 90 °C, trefoil | catalogue sheet (R already temperature-corrected) |
| Prospective fault | I_sc = 12 kA symmetric RMS, t = 0.8 s | given; 12 kA treated as the RMS symmetrical value, no DC/peak asymmetry factor |
| Thermal limits | θ_i = 90 °C, θ_f ≤ 250 °C | catalogue sheet |
| Copper | ρ20 = 1.724e-8 Ω·m, α = 0.00393 K⁻¹, δ = 8890 kg/m³, c = 385 J/kg·K | catalogue sheet |

## 2. Constraint 1 — voltage drop

ΔV = √3 · I · L · (R·cosφ + X·sinφ)

√3 · 180 A · 0.040 km = **12.471 A·km** (a common multiplier for all four cables)

| Cable | R·cosφ (Ω/km) | X·sinφ (Ω/km) | R·cosφ + X·sinφ (Ω/km) | ΔV (V) | ΔV (% of 400 V) | ≤ 12.0 V ? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V50 | 0.4397×0.85 = 0.37375 | 0.080×0.5268 = 0.04214 | 0.41589 | **5.19** | 1.30 % | yes |
| V70 | 0.3140×0.85 = 0.26690 | 0.04214 | 0.30904 | **3.85** | 0.96 % | yes |
| V95 | 0.2314×0.85 = 0.19669 | 0.04214 | 0.23883 | **2.98** | 0.74 % | yes |
| V120 | 0.1832×0.85 = 0.15572 | 0.04214 | 0.19786 | **2.47** | 0.62 % | yes |

All four catalogue cables satisfy the 3 % (12.0 V) limit. Voltage drop therefore does not discriminate between them; the largest drop (V50, 5.19 V) is still only 43 % of the permitted 12.0 V.

## 3. Constraint 2 — ampacity

Load 180 A against catalogue continuous ampacity in the stated arrangement (free air, 40 °C, trefoil). No grouping/enclosure derating factor is given, so the published values are applied directly.

- V50: 180 / 196 = 0.918 → **196 A ≥ 180 A, pass** (8.9 % margin)
- V70: 246 A ≥ 180 A, pass (27 % margin)
- V95: 301 A ≥ 180 A, pass (40 % margin; tolerable derating factor 0.598)
- V120: 352 A ≥ 180 A, pass

All four cables satisfy constraint 2.

## 4. Short-circuit thermal withstand (12 kA, 0.8 s, 90 °C → 250 °C)

Adiabatic energy balance per unit length, I²·ρ(θ)/A·dt = A·δ·c·dθ, with ρ(θ) = ρ20[1 + α(θ − 20)]:

I²·t / (δ·c·A²) = ∫dθ/ρ(θ) = J

J = [1/(ρ20·α)] · ln[ (1 + α(250−20)) / (1 + α(90−20)) ]
 = [1/(1.724e-8 × 0.00393)] · ln(1.9039 / 1.2751)
 = 1.47594e10 × 0.400818 = **5.9158e9**

k = √(δ·c·J) = √(8890 × 385 × 5.9158e9) = 1.4229e8 A·√s/m² = **142.3 A·√s/mm²**
(consistent with the IEC copper/XLPE value k = 143 for 90 → 250 °C, which validates the input data)

Fault energy: I²t = (12 000)² × 0.8 = **1.152e8 A²s**

Minimum section: A_min = I_sc·√t / k = 12 000 × 0.89443 / 142.3 = 10 733 / 142.3 = **75.4 mm²**

End temperature actually reached by each catalogue section, θ_f = 20 + { [1+α(90−20)]·exp(I²t·ρ20·α /(δ·c·A²)) − 1 } / α, with I²t·ρ20·α = 1.152e8 × 6.7753e-11 = 7.8052e-3:

| Cable | A (mm²) | δ·c·A² (kg·J/K per m) | exponent | θ_f (°C) | ≤ 250 °C ? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V50 | 50 | 8.557e-3 | 0.9122 | **573** | **no — fails** |
| V70 | 70 | 1.677e-2 | 0.4654 | **282** | **no — fails** |
| V95 | 95 | 3.089e-2 | 0.2527 | **183** | yes |
| V120 | 120 | 4.929e-2 | 0.1584 | **146** | yes |

V95 and V120 withstand the fault. V95 reaches 183 °C, i.e. 67 K below the 250 °C limit, and has 1.59× headroom in I²t (it would only reach 250 °C at I²t = 1.83e8 A²s). V70 and V50 are rejected: they exceed the short-time limit and would require replacement of the cable after a single fault at the board's prospective current.

## 5. Selection and cost

Screening of all four options against the three simultaneous constraints:

| Cable | Ampacity A | 180 A ≤ ampacity | ΔV (V) | ΔV ≤ 12.0 V | θ_f (°C) | θ_f ≤ 250 °C | Cost EUR/m | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V50 | 196 | yes | 5.19 | yes | 573 | **no** | 9.2 | rejected — fault |
| V70 | 246 | yes | 3.85 | yes | 282 | **no** | 13.4 | rejected — fault |
| **V95** | **301** | **yes** | **2.98** | **yes** | **183** | **yes** | **18.6** | **selected — lowest cost compliant** |
| V120 | 352 | yes | 2.47 | yes | 146 | yes | 24.0 | compliant, not lowest cost |

Cost comparison (single conductor, as catalogued; three-core set and 40 m run shown for completeness — ranking is identical on any of these bases):

| Cable | EUR/m (per conductor) | EUR/m (3-conductor set) | EUR per 40 m run (3 conductors) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V50 | 9.2 | 27.6 | 1 104 (non-compliant) |
| V70 | 13.4 | 40.2 | 1 608 (non-compliant) |
| V95 | 18.6 | 55.8 | **2 232 (compliant)** |
| V120 | 24.0 | 72.0 | 2 880 (compliant) |

**Selected cable: V95** — the lowest-cost catalogue option (18.6 EUR/m per conductor, 2 232 EUR for the 40 m three-core run) that simultaneously satisfies voltage drop ≤ 3 % of 400 V (2.98 V vs 12.0 V limit), ampacity (301 A vs 180 A), and 12 kA / 0.8 s adiabatic withstand (183 °C vs 250 °C limit). The cheaper V50 (9.2 EUR/m) and V70 (13.4 EUR/m) are excluded by the short-circuit thermal check only; both pass the voltage-drop and ampacity constraints.

## 6. Points to confirm before ordering

- The 12 kA is taken as the RMS symmetrical prospective current; the adiabatic check uses its I²t. If the 12 kA figure is declared to include DC offset, effective I²t rises (up to ~2× for a fully offset wave) and V95's 1.59× margin could be consumed — re-run with the asymmetrical I²t if so.
- 0.8 s is taken as the guaranteed maximum total clearing time (breaker + protection relay). Any longer declared clearing time scales A_min as √t.
- No grouping/enclosure derating factor was supplied, so the published 40 °C free-air ampacity is used as-is. V95 tolerates derating down to 0.598 before ampacity governs, so this assumption is not critical to the selection.
- Starting temperature for the fault check is the 90 °C continuous limit (worst case); a lower pre-fault temperature would give a lower θ_f.

**Selected cable: V95.**

# Kestrel motor selection — belt-driven mixer, 3600 rpm / 15 N·m process duty

Source: Northline Drives, *Kestrel three-phase motors* (document T4-55-1.md). Rated voltage 400 V. All catalogue values below are the motor-shaft ratings as published: rated torque is continuous torque at the motor shaft at rated speed, rated current is line current at that torque, mass is motor mass. No other vendor or product line is used.

## 1. Drive kinematics (pulley ratio)

- Motor pulley pitch diameter D_m = 240 mm; process-shaft pulley pitch diameter D_p = 80 mm.
- Ratio i = D_m / D_p = 240 / 80 = 3.0 — a **speed-up** from motor to process shaft (the process shaft turns three times per motor revolution).
- Required motor speed: n_m = n_p / i = 3600 / 3 = **1200 rpm**.
- This matches the rated speed of every Kestrel model exactly, so no VFD, gearbox or pulley change is required, and the motor runs at its rated operating point (best efficiency, rated cooling).

## 2. Duty point referred to the motor shaft

Process-shaft load: 15 N·m steady at 3600 rpm.

- Process power: P_p = T_p · ω_p = 15 × (2π × 3600 / 60) = **5654.9 W**
- Motor input power (belt efficiency η = 0.96): P_m = P_p / η = 5654.9 / 0.96 = **5890.5 W**
- Motor shaft torque: T_m = P_m / ω_m = 5890.5 / (2π × 1200 / 60) = **46.875 N·m**
- Direct equivalent: T_m = T_p × (D_m / D_p) / η = 15 × 3 / 0.96 = 46.875 N·m ✔ (agrees)

**Direction-of-ratio warning.** Because this is a 3:1 overdrive, the motor must supply *three times* the process torque divided by efficiency — 46.9 N·m — not one third of it. Any calculation that yields ≈5.2 N·m (15 × 80/240 / 0.96) has inverted the pulley ratio and is wrong by a factor of 9. Selecting on that basis would pick the K-20 (22 N·m), which can only deliver 22/3 × 0.96 = **7.04 N·m** at the process shaft — 47 % of the 15 N·m demanded. The mixer would stall.

## 3. Compliance screening of the full Kestrel range

Constraints: rated torque ≥ 46.9 N·m (able to drive the duty); rated current ≤ 16 A; mass ≤ 40 kg. Catalogue is the only source.

| Model | Rated torque (N·m) | Torque ≥ 46.9? | Current (A) | ≤ 16 A? | Mass (kg) | ≤ 40 kg? | Price (EUR) | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| K-20 | 22 | No | 5.5 | Yes | 18 | Yes | 640 | Reject — torque (2.76 kW shaft vs 5.89 kW required) |
| K-40 | 40 | No | 9.6 | Yes | 28 | Yes | 910 | Reject — torque (5.03 kW shaft vs 5.89 kW required) |
| **K-55** | **55** | **Yes** | **13.2** | **Yes** | **36** | **Yes** | **1280** | **Accept — cheapest compliant** |
| K-75 | 75 | Yes | 18.1 | No | 48 | No | 1710 | Reject — current (18.1 A > 16 A) and mass (48 kg > 40 kg) |

Cheapest model satisfying all three constraints: **K-55, EUR 1280**. It is the only member of the passing set, so the price comparison is trivial.

## 4. Verification of the selected motor at the duty point

- Process-shaft torque available from K-55 at rated torque: T_p,avail = 55 / 3 × 0.96 = **17.6 N·m** ≥ 15 N·m required → margin 17.6 / 15 = **1.17** (17 %).
- Process-shaft power available: 55 × 125.664 × 0.96 = 6635 W ≥ 5655 W required → load factor 5655 / 6635 = **0.85**.
- The motor therefore runs continuously (S1) at 85 % of rated torque, below its rated temperature rise — sustained duty is satisfied with no derating.
- Electrical headroom: 13.2 A ≤ 16 A, 2.8 A (17.5 %) spare; at 400 V three-phase this is ≈9.1 kVA apparent input for ≈6.9 kW shaft.
- Mass headroom: 36 kg ≤ 40 kg, 4 kg spare for the terminal box, coupling half and mounting bracket.
- Service-factor sensitivity: with a 1.15 service factor applied to the 46.9 N·m requirement (53.9 N·m) the K-55 (55 N·m) still complies. A factor of 1.25 or higher (58.6 N·m) would exceed the K-55, and the only larger model (K-75) is barred by both the 16 A and 40 kg limits — so if a ≥1.25 SF is a site requirement, the specification (not the selection logic) must be revisited. On the stated constraints no service factor applies and the K-55 is correct.
- Robustness to efficiency convention: even if the belt efficiency were multiplied rather than divided (15 × 3 × 0.96 = 43.2 N·m), the K-40 (40 N·m) still fails and the K-55 is still the cheapest compliant motor. The selection does not hinge on the efficiency convention.

## 5. Application and installation notes

- **Belt speed:** v = π · D_m · n_m / 60 = π × 0.240 × 20 = 15.1 m/s — comfortably inside normal V-belt practice (≤ ~40 m/s), so the 240 mm pulley on the 1200 rpm shaft is not a limiting feature.
- **Pulley fit:** a 240 mm pitch-diameter pulley on the motor shaft is a normal overhung load for a 36 kg frame at 1200 rpm; confirm the motor shaft diameter and keyway against the pulley bore, and align pulleys to within ~0.5 mm and <0.5° angular misalignment. Use a taper-lock or keyed bushing; do not rely on set screws alone in a reversing or high-vibration duty.
- **Guarding:** the 240 mm pulley and belt run at 15 m/s; fit a fixed guard to EN 953 / ISO 14120 before commissioning.
- **Supply check:** the catalogue gives 400 V and 1200 rpm rated. Confirm the site supply frequency; a 1200 rpm rated 6-pole machine corresponds to a 60 Hz supply. If the site is 50 Hz the actual full-load speed would be ~960 rpm and the process shaft would run at ~2880 rpm instead of 3600 rpm — the pulley ratio (not the motor choice) would then need rework. All four models share the same 1200 rpm rating, so this does not change the selection.
- **Protection:** set the overload relay to the 13.2 A nameplate current (or 1.0–1.05 × FLC for a Class 10 relay), not to the 16 A limit; 16 A is a selection ceiling, not a trip setting.

## Results

| Motor | Torque (N·m) | Speed (rpm) | Current (A) | Price (EUR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| K-55 | 55 | 1200 | 13.2 | 1280 |

## Selection of a Plainflat bar for a 90 kN static tie (Calder Sections)

### 1. Basis of calculation

| Item | Value / basis |
|---|---|
| Tensile force P | 90 kN = 90 000 N (static, working load, no partial factors applied) |
| Bar length L | 1.5 m |
| End condition | Clevis each end, one 18 mm dia. pin through one hole on the bar centreline |
| Tensile stress limit | 155 MPa |
| Density | 7850 kg/m³ (per catalogue) |
| Section area | A_gross = width × thickness (per catalogue) |
| **Governing stress basis** | **Net section through the pin hole: A_net = (b − d₀)·t with d₀ = 18 mm** |

The pin hole removes material directly from the load path, so the tensile check is made on the net section through the hole (consistent with the net-area basis used for pin-connected tension members and for clevis eyes, i.e. AISC 360 D5 / EN 1993-1-1 §6.2.2). Gross-section stresses are also tabulated below for comparison, but they are not the governing check.

σ = P / A_net = 90 000 / [(b − 18)·t]  (N, mm² → MPa)

Mass: m = A_gross × L × ρ = A × 1 500 mm × 7850 kg/m³ × 10⁻⁹

Material removed by the two pin holes (2 × π/4 × 18² × t = 5 089 mm³ for t = 10 mm) is 0.04 kg — about 0.4 % of the bar mass — and is neglected; the tabulated masses are therefore conservative (gross bar), consistent with the 20 kg limit being a gross-mass limit.

### 2. Geometry screen (width ≥ 40 mm, thickness ≥ 6 mm)

All four catalogue bars pass: widths 60/70/80/80 mm (all ≥ 40), thicknesses 10/10/10/12 mm (all ≥ 6). The geometry limits therefore do not discriminate between the candidates.

### 3. Net-section tensile check (σ ≤ 155 MPa)

| Model | b (mm) | t (mm) | A_gross (mm²) | A_net = (b−18)t (mm²) | σ_net (MPa) | Verdict | σ_gross (MPa) (comparison) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| PF-60x10 | 60 | 10 | 600 | 420 | 214.3 | **FAIL** (> 155) | 150.0 |
| PF-70x10 | 70 | 10 | 700 | 520 | 173.1 | **FAIL** (> 155) | 128.6 |
| PF-80x10 | 80 | 10 | 800 | 620 | **145.2** | **PASS** | 112.5 |
| PF-80x12 | 80 | 12 | 960 | 744 | 121.0 | PASS | 93.8 |

Worked check for the selected bar, PF-80x10:

- A_net = (80 − 18) × 10 = 620 mm²
- σ = 90 000 / 620 = 145.16 → **145.2 MPa** ≤ 155 MPa ✔ (utilisation 145.2/155 = 0.937)

(PF-60x10 would pass on gross area at 150.0 MPa, but it fails on the net section at 214.3 MPa — the hole, not the gross bar, governs. PF-70x10 likewise fails at 173.1 MPa net.)

### 4. Mass check (m ≤ 20 kg at 1.5 m)

| Model | A_gross (mm²) | Volume (mm³) | Mass (kg) | ≤ 20 kg? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PF-60x10 | 600 | 900 000 | 7.07 | yes |
| PF-70x10 | 700 | 1 050 000 | 8.24 | yes |
| PF-80x10 | 800 | 1 200 000 | **9.42** | **yes** |
| PF-80x12 | 960 | 1 440 000 | 11.30 | yes |

Worked check: m = 800 mm² × 1500 mm × 7850 kg/m³ × 10⁻⁹ = 9.42 kg ≤ 20 kg ✔

The 20 kg limit is not binding for any catalogue bar; it only rules out bars far heavier than the largest Plainflat section.

### 5. Selection

Ranking the bars that satisfy the net-section stress limit by mass:

1. **PF-80x10 — 9.42 kg, 145.2 MPa, 80 mm wide** ← lightest compliant bar
2. PF-80x12 — 11.30 kg, 121.0 MPa, 80 mm wide (heavier, so not selected; lower stress is not the stated objective)

PF-60x10 (7.07 kg) and PF-70x10 (8.24 kg) are lighter but exceed 155 MPa on the net section through the 18 mm pin hole and are therefore rejected.

**Selected bar: PF-80x10**, 80 mm × 10 mm, 1.5 m long, mass 9.42 kg, net-section tensile stress 145.2 MPa.

Edge distance check for the selected bar (informational): clear material each side of the hole = (80 − 18)/2 = 31 mm = 1.72 d₀, comfortably above the usual 0.75 d₀ edge-distance minimum for pin connections, so the 80 mm width is adequate around a centred 18 mm hole.

### 6. Items outside the stated criteria (not scored here)

The request specifies only the tensile stress limit, the width/thickness minimums and the mass limit, so only those are used for selection. The following are joint checks that depend on data not given in the request (bar steel grade, pin and clevis material, end distance to the bar ends, hole clearance) and are **not** part of this selection:

- Bearing at the pin hole (P/(d₀·t) = 90 000/(18 × 10) = 500 MPa for PF-80x10) and shear tear-out to the bar ends — to be verified against the pin/clevis and bar material allowables.
- Pin shear and pin bending across the clevis gap; clevis ear net section.
- Hole clearance/fit, hole finish, and any end shaping or machining that would alter finished mass.
- Dimensional tolerances on supplied width/thickness (the selected bar has 6.3 % stress margin, so a −6 % area tolerance would exhaust it; specify mill tolerance or order with the stress check reconfirmed if tolerances are wide).
- Whether the 90 kN is characteristic or factored — the 155 MPa limit is applied directly to the 90 kN working load as stated, with no additional partial factors.

## Selection calculation

Given a 400 V, 50 Hz feeder and a load of 75 kVA at 0.8 lagging power factor, the load current is

I_load = S / (√3 × V) = 75,000 / (√3 × 400) = 108.25 A ≈ 108.3 A.

The 0.8 power factor sets the phase angle but does not change the apparent-power current magnitude. With reactor winding resistance negligible, the voltage drop is the quadrature I·X drop.

The Bay catalogue defines x as per-unit reactance on a 100 kVA base at rated voltage. For a load S on that base, the per-unit voltage drop is

Δu_pu = x × (S / S_base) = x × (75 / 100) = 0.75x.

As a percentage: Δu_% = 75x.

Equivalently, the reactance in ohms is X = x × V² / S_base = x × 400² / 100,000 = 1.6x Ω, and the per-phase drop is I_load × X; expressed as a percentage of phase voltage this gives the same 75x%.
